Sam L: Quick question — when we seal bundles for air-gapped installs, do we have a firm ordering guarantee for seal/unseal metadata application? I worry about partial unseals during interrupted applies.
Anya P: Short answer: no absolute global ordering today. We apply per-component activation markers; unseal happens component-by-component. Why? performance + parallelism.
Kevin T: We saw a bug last week where the verifier unsealed a component before its dependency was activated, causing service to crash on startup. We need a plan.
Maria S: Repro steps? logs?
Kevin T: From onprem node #42: "failed to start service X: missing config Y (expected from comp-B)"
Kevin T: The sequence was: download -> verify -> unpack -> unseal(comp-A) -> activate(comp-A) -> unpack(comp-B) -> activate(comp-B). comp-A depended on comp-B config. So ordering mismatch.
Anya P: Huh. That implies our manifest dependency graph isn't fully respected during activation. We currently only use manifest edges for download ordering. Activation is per-operator parallel.
Sam L: Proposal: extend manifest with an activation-phase DAG and a lightweight "activation-preconditions" entry per component. Agent respects these preconditions before unseal/activate.
Maria S: Activation-preconditions could be labels like "needs-config-from: comp-B" or simple hash refs. Then agent would wait for a marker file for comp-B activation.
Kevin T: That works but increases latency for large bundles — could block the whole apply if we wait synchronously.
Anya P: We should allow two modes: strict activation (wait on preconditions) and optimistic activation (start but stay in init-state and re-check). Operator can pick via policy.
Sam L: Also need to ensure markers are durable across restarts and idempotent. Use content-addressed marker files under /var/lib/rw/activation-markers/<digest> with signed metadata.
Maria S: We also need to handle rollback: if comp-B fails after comp-A activated, comp-A should either revert or move to degraded. Define a "quarantine" activation mode.
Kevin T: Agree. Suggested states: pending -> activating -> activated -> quarantined -> rolled_back. Agent needs clear state transitions and timeouts.
deploy-bot: RFC: seal-unseal-activation: added to docs repo — https://gitlab.redwood/internal/rfcs/SEAL-UNSEAL-2026
Anya P: One more: metadata compatibility. If we change activation schema (activation-preconditions), old agents should still be able to apply new bundles for a transition period.
Sam L: Backwards compatibility plan: new bundles include a "compatibility shim" that contains a minimal legacy activation ordering manifest (flattened list) derived from the DAG. Old agents use the flattened list; new agents prefer DAG.
Maria S: That increases bundle size slightly but it's predictable. We can version the manifest: manifest.v1 (legacy), manifest.v2 (dag). Agent reads highest supported.
Kevin T: Security: ensure shim doesn't enable TOCTOU. All activation manifests must be included inside the signed envelope; agent must validate signature before trusting ordering.
Anya P: We'll also add a verification step: the signer must assert the activation graph hash in the envelope root. That prevents post-signing reorder.
Sam L: Action items: 1) write RFC with activation-preconditions + states + policy modes, 2) prototype marker file approach on agent (Maria+Kevin), 3) draft transition plan for existing onprem fleets (Anya). I'll own RFC.
Maria S: Happy to pair on prototype. I'll start a branch with marker proof-of-concept.
Kevin T: I'll add unit tests for restart durability and a simulate-failure test to verify quarantine/rollback.
Anya P: I'll draft a rollout playbook: prefer new bundles with flattened shim for first 2 months, monitor activations/rollbacks.
Sam L: Thanks. Quick poll: thumbs up if we proceed with manifest.v2 + shim for v1 compatibility.
Maria S: :thumbsup:
Kevin T: :thumbsup:
Anya P: :thumbsup:
Sam L: Great. I'll post the RFC this afternoon.
